name: the Douglas E. Dayton Arboretum
title: Ancient Trees in East Hampton's Dayton Arboretum: 6 to Find
meta_description: A former mayor's garden of labelled specimen trees beside Herrick Park. Six trees in East Hampton, from a zelkova that fills the car park to a southern magnolia.
intro: The Douglas E. Dayton Arboretum is a former mayor's garden of specimen trees beside Herrick Park in East Hampton, which the town now owns, and many of its trees carry a small black label with the name. That is how a reader knew the royal paulownia, which most gardens keep slim and this one has let grow, and the Sawara cypress of the form 'Squarrosa', usually a border shrub, that has become a tree beside a bench. The sourwood, a tree of the eastern United States that is normally modest and grows in the shade of bigger ones, is large enough here to make a reader look up. A southern magnolia, a tree of the warm coastal South, grows alone on open grass beside the ball fields on Long Island and has made a broad, full crown. A Japanese zelkova fills the sky above two parked cars, its leaves spilling onto the tarmac in November. A many-stemmed beech, which the reader took for a ginkgo, turns copper and gold in the same month. All six came from readers, so no ages are claimed.
